newsitem.title: USA: Indianapolis arena bills head for final vote.
newsitem.headline: Indianapolis arena bills head for final vote.

text.p: Legislation to help finance a new arena for the Indiana Pacers basketball arena could be taken up as early as next week by the Indiana Senate for a final vote, according to the Senate Republican majority communications office.
The bills, which would allow Indianapolis to raise or expand existing taxes and create a professional sports development district in its downtown, passed the Senate Finance Committee on Thursday.
The bills were approved earlier this month by the House, according to Gail Brown, manager of business communications for Indianapolis.
The city plans to use an estimated $5 million in annual sales and income taxes generated within the sports district to back bonds for a $175 million basketball arena, Brown said.

Indianapolis' share of the project has been pegged at $55 million, while another $50 million is being sought from private sources, including a group of 19 area businesses that invested in the bond-financed Circle Centre Mall in the city's downtown, she added.
"They are discussing the possibility of the city taking over their portion of ownership in the mall and (the businesses) investing in the arena," Brown said.
The Pacers are expected to contribute $30 million to the arena project, which would still be $40 million short of its estimated price tag.

The legislation would also allow a hike in the city's hotel-motel tax to six percent from five percent and the car rental tax to six percent from four percent. The bill also expands the application of a five percent ticket tax to raise about $2 million annually.

Brown said revenues from the hotel-motel and car rental tax hikes would largely fund a $40 million expansion of the city's convention center, although some excess revenues could be used for the arena.
